newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Navy to give up historic cemetery - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Navy to give up historic cemetery - report.

text.p: The United States Navy was to give away a historic cemetery plot in Key West, Fla., the last resting place of sailors killed in the 1898 explosion of the battleship Maine in Havana harbour, the Miami Herald reported on Friday.

The unexplained Feb. 15, 1898 explosion -- blamed at the time on enemy sabotage -- sank the Maine and triggered the Spanish-American War, in which Spain lost its last significant colonies of Cuba and the Philippines to the United States.

The Herald quoted Chief Karl Stahl of the Key West Naval Air Station as saying the decision was made by the U.S. Congress, not the Navy, following a 1994-95 review by an independent panel of the Navy's Key West properties.
The review found the plot to be surplus to Navy requirements, the Herald said.

The plot, in a fenced-off section of Key West Cemetery, is the last resting place of 24 sailors, only seven of whom were ever identified. The Herald said the Navy would hand the plot over to Key West city authorities.
Officials in Key West were not immediately available for comment.
